name: Common Variable Immunodeficiency

ethnicAssociations: Rare in Asian and African populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ESID/PAGID Revised Diagnostic Criteria for CVID

criteria.description: Marked decrease of IgG (at least 2 SD below mean for age) with low IgA and/or low IgM
Onset of immunodeficiency after age 4 years (to exclude congenital agammaglobulinemia)
Absent isohemagglutinins and/or poor response to vaccines
Exclusion of other defined causes of hypogammaglobulinemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All four major criteria must be met. CVID is a diagnosis of exclusion after ruling out secondary causes and monogenic immune deficiencies.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: CVID is the most common symptomatic primary immunodeficiency in adults. Diagnostic delay averages 4-9 years from symptom onset. A subset of patients have identified monogenic defects (TNFRSF13B/TACI, ICOS, BAFFR, etc.).

common.notes: Often from Giardia, norovirus, or nodular lymphoid hyperplasia

occasional.symptomName: Non-caseating granulomas (lung, liver, spleen, lymph nodes)

laboratory: Low serum IgG (typically <500 mg/dL, often <300 mg/dL)
Poor antibody response to protein and polysaccharide vaccines
Abnormal B cell subsets on flow cytometry (reduced switched memory B cells)
May have associated cytopenias, elevated inflammatory markers
imaging: CT chest showing bronchiectasis, interstitial lung disease, or granulomatous disease
CT abdomen may show nodular lymphoid hyperplasia in GI tract
genetic: NFKB1, NFKB2, PIK3CD, CTLA4, LRBA mutations in CVID-like phenotypes
Most cases are sporadic; ~10-25% have family history
other: Vaccine challenge: measure specific antibody titers before and 4-6 weeks after immunization
B cell flow cytometry panel (important for classification)
GI endoscopy may show villous atrophy, nodular lymphoid hyperplasia
Liver biopsy if hepatic granulomatous disease suspected

distinguishingFeatures: Only IgA is deficient; IgG and IgM normal
Presents in infancy (after maternal antibody wanes)
Very low or absent B cells
Associated with nephrotic syndrome (urinary protein loss)

redFlags: Recurrent pneumonia leading to bronchiectasis and progressive lung damage
Granulomatous-lymphocytic interstitial lung disease (GLILD) with progressive respiratory failure
Severe autoimmune cytopenias refractory to treatment
Chronic enteropathy with malabsorption and weight loss
references: Bonilla FA, et al. Practice parameter for the diagnosis and management of primary immunodeficiency. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2015;136(5):1186-1205.e78.
Cunningham-Rundles C. Common variable immune deficiency: case studies. Blood. 2019;134(21):1787-1795.
Chapel H, et al. Common variable immunodeficiency disorders: division into distinct clinical phenotypes. Blood. 2008;112(2):277-286.
Gathmann B, et al. Clinical picture and treatment of 2212 patients with common variable immunodeficiency. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2014;134(1):116-126.
